guidance: All water work is breaststroke except the explicitly optional backstroke recovery lengths.
Rest is after each repetition, not a send-off. Take longer when needed and restart only when breathing has settled.
On an amber day—heavy legs, repeated gasping, broken timing, or lingering fatigue—replace fast and speed-assist work with easy 25s. Never make up missed metres.

If easy 50s cause marked breathlessness, split them into 2 × 25 m with 20–30 seconds extra rest. Stop for unusual breathlessness, wheezing, chest discomfort, or dizziness and seek appropriate medical advice.
Stop breaststroke kick work if your knees or groin hurt and tell your coach. Do not train through pain.
No breath-hold sets, hyperventilation, underwater time or distance targets, or forced kick counts. All swimming and starts are supervised.

days.title: Baseline + distance per stroke
days.focus: Record your average stroke count per 25 m as the baseline for this block.

sets.name: Kick + pull drill
sets.cue: Use a board for kick-only and a buoy with no kick for pull-only.

sets.name: Distance per stroke
sets.cue: Count strokes. Hold or lower the count while keeping the same easy-to-controlled pace.

sets.name: Turn technique
sets.cue: Focus on approach, two-hand touch and a quick tuck—not speed.

days.title: Endurance + tempo
days.focus: Hold your form into the second half and finish stronger without losing rhythm.

sets.name: Tempo build
sets.cue: 25 m body-dolphin-kick-and-glide + 25 m breaststroke pull with a light flutter kick.

sets.name: Negative-split endurance
sets.cue: First 50 steady (5–6/10), second 50 faster (7–8/10). Finish strong, not exhausted.

days.title: Race-pace 25s + dive sprints
days.focus: Connect a flat start, legal pullout, and immediate race-speed swimming.

sets.name: Timing-pause drill
sets.cue: Pause 1–2 seconds in full streamline between cycles; let the final rep flow at race effort.

sets.name: Dive sprints
sets.cue: Supervised start or push. Legal pullout and tight streamline to the first breakout.

sets.name: Race-pace 25s
sets.cue: Use intended race stroke rate. Stop early if two reps in a row fade by about one second.

days.title: Turn speed + controlled 50
days.focus: Make the turn quick and legal while keeping the full 50 controlled.

sets.name: Technique drill
sets.cue: Choose distance-per-stroke or timing-pause work based on what needs attention today.

sets.name: Fast turns
sets.cue: Swim the final 10 m into the wall at 8/10, execute the full turn at speed, then ease out.

sets.name: Full-50 rehearsal
sets.cue: Start, turn and finish at 7/10. This is a routine run-through, not a max effort.

days.title: Rest
days.focus: Full rest day. No drills and no make-up training.

days.title: Easy technique + recovery
days.focus: No fast work. Leave the pool fresher than you arrived.

days.title: Max test + broken 100
days.focus: Record the 50 m time, first-25 split, and stroke count. Do one maximal 50 only.

sets.name: Warm-up
sets.cue: Easy breaststroke; build the final two reps to controlled.

sets.name: Start rehearsal
sets.cue: Supervised start, then easy after the breakout.

sets.name: Max test
sets.cue: Full race: start, turn and finish. Record the 25 m split and stroke count; do not repeat it.

sets.name: Broken 100
sets.rest: 10 s between 25s · 3 min after the set
sets.cue: Hold your 50 m race pace through all four lengths.

days.title: Race pace + turn combo
days.focus: Keep race stroke rate connected through the turn without turning the session into a test.

sets.name: Full-50 rehearsal
sets.cue: Start, turn and finish at a controlled 8/10 with full attention on the turn.

days.title: Easy recovery
days.focus: No fast work. The short distance is deliberate.

days.title: Sharpen: short max + starts
days.focus: This is the final genuinely hard speed session.

sets.name: Starts
sets.cue: Supervised start, max for the first 15 m, then hold form to the wall.

days.title: Final controlled rehearsal
days.focus: Rehearse the routine calmly. Do not add extra sprints.

sets.name: Full-race sequence
sets.cue: Run the familiar start-to-finish sequence at 7/10. This is not a time trial.

days.title: Rest
days.focus: Full rest. Prepare your bag, cap, goggles and suit; eat and rest normally.

days.title: Pre-race activation
days.focus: Keep it short and sharp. Skip the session if you feel unwell or unusually fatigued.

days.title: 50 m breaststroke competition
days.focus: Flat entry, patient pullout, head-first breakout, fast turn, and strong tempo to the touch.
days.distanceLabel: 400 m warm-up · 50 m race · 100 m cool-down
days.note: Use the meet timetable, not the normal pool window. Adapt the warm-up to lane access and your coach’s guidance.

sets.name: Timing-pause drill
sets.cue: Relaxed timing and a clean body line.

sets.name: Start + burst
sets.cue: Start if allowed, otherwise push. Max for the first 15 m, then ease down.

raceCues: Drive out low and flat, lock the streamline, complete one legal pullout, and break out head first.
Build into a fast, connected breaststroke rhythm without shortening into panic.
Touch with both hands together and separated, snap the tuck, and drive the push-off straight back.
Hold tempo through the final 10 m and finish on a fast two-hand touch—do not glide in.
days.after: If a cool-down lane is available and you feel comfortable, swim 4 × 25 m very easy. Record your time, 25 m splits, stroke counts, whether the start/turn/finish were legal, and one cue for next time.

efforts.CONTROLLED: 5–7/10. Purposeful work with technique fully intact.
efforts.QUICK: 8/10. Fast and clean, with generous recovery.
efforts.MAX: 10/10 only for one short rep of 25 m or less, or the single planned 50 m test, with full recovery.

techniques: Pull and breathe, recover the hands forward, then kick into a long body line. Use a brief natural glide when easy and a quicker connected rhythm at race effort.
Turn the feet outward through the propulsive phase. Keep it comfortable and coordinated; never force a wide knee position. Stop for knee or groin pain.
Count strokes per 25 m. Aim for fewer strokes at the same or better time—not more effort.
At race effort, use a faster connected turnover: shorter strokes taken quickly, not long strokes rushed.
Enter flat and shallow in a locked streamline. One arm pull and one optional legal dolphin kick may precede the breaststroke kick. Surface sooner whenever needed; underwater distance is not the goal.
Arrive on the fastest part of the stroke, touch with both hands together and separated, release one hand immediately, tuck quickly, and push straight back before the legal pullout.
Keep your tempo through the wall and make a simultaneous, separated two-hand touch at speed rather than gliding in.
